hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce with global artist residency program
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as a vibrant artistic hub by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting artists from around the world. The non-profit organization maintains the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the former owners whose influence still shapes the property today. According to the foundation, the estate remains approximately 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there, reflecting their original vision and taste. Guided tours of the lush gardens and distinctive architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for visitors interested in exploring this unique landmark.

Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship defines much of the estate's character. His tilework extends throughout the entire facility, visible on floors, walls, and ceilings. The property includes a smoking and bourbon room featuring masculine paneling and pre-stained glass that opens onto a patio bar. The Crains' nine international travels resulted in a collection of one-of-a-kind items that decorate the estate, including a gazebo shipped from India adorned with tiny peacocks. The foundation has prioritized keeping these original elements intact rather than pursuing commercial development.

The estate's most famous residents are its peacocks, birds the Crains are believed to have introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. Starting with seven birds, the population has grown to over 100 peacocks roaming the property. Among them is Bob, a beloved peacock estimated to be 60 years old and distinguished by a noticeable limp. Bob lives inside the estate and enjoys daily hand-feedings from his own bowls. Tour guides highlight that children feeding peacocks directly from their hands creates memorable experiences for young visitors.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program attracting creative professionals from across the globe and providing simple yet elegant accommodations on the grounds. The art lab, directed by Krystal Masters, offers classes in sculpting, watercolor, and other mediums designed for both children and adults regardless of experience level. Masters emphasizes that most of her classes are one-on-one sessions where students arrive with no prior experience and leave with completed artwork. She views art as therapeutic, noting that it allows people to disconnect from their phones and leave feeling good. Her own work includes a sculpture of her brother's tuxedo cat wearing a tuxedo, and she regularly hosts workshops like "paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow." For Masters, the most rewarding aspect of her role is watching students depart fulfilled and enriched by their artistic experience.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on SR-710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane.

The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was transported via Lifestar from the scene.

The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash. The identities of the drivers have not been released.

cards.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that would have raised damages caps for government negligence victims
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis vetoed legislation that would have increased damages caps for people injured by government negligence, rejecting the first such increase to pass the Florida Legislature in 16 years. The measure, HB 145, earned overwhelming bipartisan support when it passed in March but faced rejection on Monday. DeSantis argued that raising the caps would encourage unmeritorious lawsuits. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. "I have no question or doubt that that would happen."

The bill, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Rep. Fiona McFarland with a companion measure from Lake Mary Republican Sen. Jason Brodeur, targeted Florida's sovereign immunity statutes, which limit compensation for government carelessness. The legislation would have raised damages caps from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident. These caps had remained unchanged since 2010. The bill would have also permitted local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding those caps without seeking legislative approval. Currently, victims seeking payments above the caps must secure passage of a special claims bill through the Legislature. The measure was scheduled to take effect October 1.

McFarland has championed the issue for three years, framing it as an equal protection matter. She argues the current system creates vastly different outcomes depending on whether someone is harmed by a government entity or a private company. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness. That doesn't sit right with me." She acknowledged local government opposition over increased liability and insurance premiums but maintained the update was necessary.

DeSantis defended the current system by pointing to claims bills approved this year. The state considers roughly a dozen such measures annually, benefiting people physically harmed by government negligence or wrongly incarcerated exonerees. This year, just over one-third of 14 filed measures cleared both chambers, with success rates varying significantly in recent years. The Florida Justice Association criticized the veto, calling it a disservice to families seeking accountability. The group's president, Chris Ligoti, noted that under the current system, compensation can take years or over a decade to arrive. It remains unclear whether McFarland or Brodeur will refile the legislation when a new governor takes office in 2027.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated after prominent DeSantis communications veterans traced them to phone and email information matching Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, publicly accused Layla Collins of operating anonymous X accounts that promoted Jay Collins and attacked those who did not endorse him, including Governor DeSantis. Promota CEO Robert Salvador shared evidence showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to ones known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication messages. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which also appeared tied to Layla Collins, noting that its content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him.

Redfern confirmed that the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their public criticisms. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, helping the former state Senator develop a statewide profile to run for Governor. DeSantis has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race because he cannot seek a third term due to term limits. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. Florida Politics has requested comment from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Supreme Court preserves grace period laws for counting absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, providing clarity for Florida election administrators.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The decision preserves grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Wetzel, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count if they bear an Election Day postmark.

A panel of three Trump-appointed 5th Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the three liberal Justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. States retain authority to set their own receipt deadlines, meaning grace period laws in roughly 30 states are protected. Florida does not have a general postmark grace period, as state law requires mail ballots in hand by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

cards.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with Venus due to knee injury
cards.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday because of a right knee injury suffered during her singles return earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. In a three-set loss to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday, the 44-year-old Williams was injured. "I'm heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles. Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," Serena said in an Instagram post. The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in a first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus, 46, competed in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again soon, telling fans to "stay tuned to a city near you." The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
hero.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, buns have risen 7.7%, and ice cream is up 5.3%. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, with prices climbing 12.4%.

Not all items on the cookout menu have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or salad. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals for groceries on your list and reducing food waste by starting with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Delray Beach elementary school jumps from 'C' to 'A' rating
cards.teaser: S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a 'C' rating last year to an 'A' this year, reflecting a turnaround effort led by Principal Rona Tata.
cards.body:
S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach jumped from a 'C' rating to an 'A' rating this year, part of the School District of Palm Beach County's third consecutive 'A' rating from the state. Principal Rona Tata, who has spent the last 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround effort.

Tata said the school had an A rating two years ago and narrowly missed a B rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, she said staff began taking a closer look at the foundation of student learning by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, according to Tata, which contributed to the renewed A rating.

Community member Chris Ceasar, who attended Spady as a child and now has family members enrolled there, said the A rating is a big thing for the community because education is first in Delray Beach. S.D. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a 'C' rating to an 'A' this year, including Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to South Florida roads
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday, with 61.4 million making the trip by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are feeling the impact. Heavy rain is adding to the challenge on already-crowded roads, with Friday's wet weather making for difficult conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Experiences on the road have varied widely. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported smooth sailing, saying they didn't see any traffic, no accidents or anything. Meanwhile, driver Fernando Amado described a very different experience, noting it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County has earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, representing 84% of the district's schools, received either an "A" or "B" rating, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. Schools and districts receive letter grades based on several factors, including student performance on state tests, graduation rates, and student performance on advanced coursework. District leaders reported that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the most notable achievements came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which improved from a "C" rating to an "A" in a single year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years after serving five years as assistant principal, spearheaded the improvement effort. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and integrates with kindergarten. Students who went through this revised program are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue responds to 29 fires overnight during Fourth of July
hero.teaser: Fire crews responded to 29 fires across Palm Beach County during the overnight hours of the Fourth of July holiday, with brush fires and trash fires accounting for most incidents.
hero.body: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue responded to 29 fires across the county during overnight hours on the Fourth of July holiday, with crews dispatched to the fires between 8 p.m. Saturday and 2 a.m., officials said. Of the 29 fires, 11 were brush fires, 15 involved trash or dumpsters, 2 were structure fires, and one was miscellaneous. Firefighters quickly contained every fire, and no major property damage was reported. The department is reminding residents who continue to celebrate the holiday weekend to do so safely and responsibly.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida community selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, becoming the only Florida city selected among 10 U.S. communities chosen this year. The award was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders presented Riviera Beach's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through long-term efforts to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars," Lawson said. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three programs designed to increase civic participation. The Riviera Beach Youth Council helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative, has a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Miller-Anderson said the city is doing innovative things to make sure the community can say they are part of what is happening in Riviera Beach. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council to vote on land transfer for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Midway Road and Florida's Turnpike. Final approval will come at an upcoming meeting.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city. The project will accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are working on the first phase widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027.

The partial interchange for the Turnpike is still in the design phase according to the FDOT website. Resident Erin Scheumeister said construction has been difficult to avoid but she believes the expansion is necessary and will make it easier to get to work. FDOT said the Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance company deny coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Her insurer, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, said the surgical mesh is investigational and not FDA-approved for breast reconstruction.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and has "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that GalaFlex's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Billington has joined doctors taking their frustrations to social media and calling out insurers by name. Last year, after an investigative series by reporter Katie LaGrone and photojournalist Matthew Apthorp, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark had her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex a little more than a week ago. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation attracts global artists to Fort Pierce with residency program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce is transforming the city into an artistic destination through its artist-in-residency program and art classes. The foundation operates on the historic Crain Estate where Jaxson and Mary Crain once lived.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation, located on the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce's Peacock Arts District, preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters on July 1 after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway. Both occupants were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat until help arrived.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life, and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely and pride in the swift response by Marine Unit deputies.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss and what made White memorable. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Adding to the heartbreak, White's birthday is July 4, so she passed just a few days before her birthday. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation that doubles slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project designed to nearly double its capacity. The work is projected to take one year, with completion expected by next Fourth of July. When finished, the dock will expand from 18 slips to 44 slips, accommodating both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. A state grant and transportation impact fees are funding the project.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve purposes beyond adding capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be able to continue operations. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for the company, said the city is allowing the business to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock for passenger boarding and drop-off. Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance to Stuart's character and economy, saying "Stuart is not Stuart without the water."

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 Friday in a World Cup match that went to extra time, with the winning goal coming off a deflection in the 111th minute.
cards.body:
Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 with a 3-2 victory over Cape Verde on Friday in South Florida. The go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Messi scored in the 29th minute for a 1-0 lead, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense as Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha. The goal was Messi's 20th career World Cup goal, extending his own record.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd. Goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football aims for state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is setting its sights on a state title heading into the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. A second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to pursue deeper postseason success. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

The Scots have scheduled more challenging opponents this fall to compete at a higher level and attract new talent. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete." For the team, success is defined by postseason advancement. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that regular season performance is secondary to playoff progress, stating advancement past the second round is the primary goal. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described summer workouts as daily motivation for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. During nesting season, the center's education and research departments work together to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse hosted Independence Day activities on July 4, including a pool party, live music and fireworks to mark the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers said this years event also recognized Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests enjoyed a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar.

Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families took part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign began around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course offered one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse also hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that would have raised damages caps for government negligence victims
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis vetoed legislation that would have increased damages caps for people injured by government negligence, rejecting the first such increase to pass the Florida Legislature in 16 years. The measure, HB 145, earned overwhelming bipartisan support when it passed in March but faced rejection on Monday. DeSantis argued that raising the caps would encourage unmeritorious lawsuits. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. "I have no question or doubt that that would happen."

The bill, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Rep. Fiona McFarland with a companion measure from Lake Mary Republican Sen. Jason Brodeur, targeted Florida's sovereign immunity statutes, which limit compensation for government carelessness. The legislation would have raised damages caps from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident. These caps had remained unchanged since 2010. The bill would have also permitted local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding those caps without seeking legislative approval. Currently, victims seeking payments above the caps must secure passage of a special claims bill through the Legislature. The measure was scheduled to take effect October 1.

McFarland has championed the issue for three years, framing it as an equal protection matter. She argues the current system creates vastly different outcomes depending on whether someone is harmed by a government entity or a private company. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness. That doesn't sit right with me." She acknowledged local government opposition over increased liability and insurance premiums but maintained the update was necessary.

DeSantis defended the current system by pointing to claims bills approved this year. The state considers roughly a dozen such measures annually, benefiting people physically harmed by government negligence or wrongly incarcerated exonerees. This year, just over one-third of 14 filed measures cleared both chambers, with success rates varying significantly in recent years. The Florida Justice Association criticized the veto, calling it a disservice to families seeking accountability. The group's president, Chris Ligoti, noted that under the current system, compensation can take years or over a decade to arrive. It remains unclear whether McFarland or Brodeur will refile the legislation when a new governor takes office in 2027.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous accounts attacking governor
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated after prominent DeSantis communications veterans traced them to phone and email information matching Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, publicly accused Layla Collins of operating anonymous X accounts that promoted Jay Collins and attacked those who did not endorse him, including Governor DeSantis. Promota CEO Robert Salvador shared evidence showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to ones known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication messages. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which also appeared tied to Layla Collins, noting that its content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him.

Redfern confirmed that the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their public criticisms. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, helping the former state Senator develop a statewide profile to run for Governor. DeSantis has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race because he cannot seek a third term due to term limits. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. Florida Politics has requested comment from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: FEMA awards $7.2 million to four Florida municipalities for Hurricane Ian infrastructure projects
cards.teaser: FloridaCommerce announced a new round of grants to help communities impacted by Hurricane Ian in September 2022, bringing total Ian recovery funding to more than $12 million.
cards.body:
FloridaCommerce is distributing $7.2 million in Hurricane Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program funds to four municipalities four years after the Category 4 storm hit Florida in September 2022. The FEMA grants fulfill local match requirements for infrastructure repairs and recovery while improving emergency preparedness and reducing the impact of future storms. Secretary of Commerce J. Alex Kelly said Florida communities are receiving the support needed to bolster critical infrastructure and storm readiness.

Charlotte County will receive $5.83 million for a public works hurricane-safe room generator and $93,392 for a leachate waste plant generator project. The Port of the Islands Community Improvement District has $750,840 for a Union Road water storage and infrastructure retrofit project. Seminole County will receive $319,437 for a mitigation reconstruction project on Shad Lane, and the city of Palatka will get $283,996 for a lift station generator. The Ian HMGMP program has already distributed more than $12 million in grants to municipalities. FEMA requires local governments to match the same amount of local funding to complete the projects.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Byrd asks court to keep Paula Stark off ballot after filing deadline error
cards.teaser: Five state employees dispute St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark's account of a paperwork mix-up that left her missing a required Form 6 less than 30 minutes before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep Paula Stark off the ballot, disputing her claims about a paperwork mix-up that disqualified her from the House District 47 race. Five state employees gave sworn written declarations saying Stark's Treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6 disclosure of financial interests and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted the rest of the paperwork less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12. Byrd argued that had Stark or Davis exercised care by questioning why the Form 6 was allegedly returned, or had Davis not waited until the final hour to submit documents, the missing form could have been submitted before the deadline. Three weeks after the qualifying deadline passed, Stark still had not submitted a Form 6, according to Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve.

Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in a Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve detailed Stark's history of paperwork problems, including late campaign finance reports, excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark stays off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 opens to all voters, who will choose between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republican filed to run in the traditionally blue seat covering parts of Osceola and Orange counties.

cards.headline: Supreme Court preserves grace period laws for counting absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, providing clarity for Florida election administrators.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The decision preserves grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Wetzel, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count if they bear an Election Day postmark.

A panel of three Trump-appointed 5th Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the three liberal Justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. States retain authority to set their own receipt deadlines, meaning grace period laws in roughly 30 states are protected. Florida does not have a general postmark grace period, as state law requires mail ballots in hand by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

cards.headline: U.S. men's national soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup Round of 16 after historic knockout victory
cards.teaser: The United States earned its first knockout stage victory since 2002 with a 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, but will face Belgium without star player Folarin Balogun, who was red-carded.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, having dispatched Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night. The team played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time of that match with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on what was widely viewed as a controversial call. Longtime referee Andy Davies told ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card. The American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie said he thought the call was a bit bogus. Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands.

Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the United States, including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup. The team is well-coached, physically capable, and playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce with global artist residency program
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as a vibrant artistic hub by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting artists from around the world. The non-profit organization maintains the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the former owners whose influence still shapes the property today. According to the foundation, the estate remains approximately 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there, reflecting their original vision and taste. Guided tours of the lush gardens and distinctive architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for visitors interested in exploring this unique landmark.

Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship defines much of the estate's character. His tilework extends throughout the entire facility, visible on floors, walls, and ceilings. The property includes a smoking and bourbon room featuring masculine paneling and pre-stained glass that opens onto a patio bar. The Crains' nine international travels resulted in a collection of one-of-a-kind items that decorate the estate, including a gazebo shipped from India adorned with tiny peacocks. The foundation has prioritized keeping these original elements intact rather than pursuing commercial development.

The estate's most famous residents are its peacocks, birds the Crains are believed to have introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. Starting with seven birds, the population has grown to over 100 peacocks roaming the property. Among them is Bob, a beloved peacock estimated to be 60 years old and distinguished by a noticeable limp. Bob lives inside the estate and enjoys daily hand-feedings from his own bowls. Tour guides highlight that children feeding peacocks directly from their hands creates memorable experiences for young visitors.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program attracting creative professionals from across the globe and providing simple yet elegant accommodations on the grounds. The art lab, directed by Krystal Masters, offers classes in sculpting, watercolor, and other mediums designed for both children and adults regardless of experience level. Masters emphasizes that most of her classes are one-on-one sessions where students arrive with no prior experience and leave with completed artwork. She views art as therapeutic, noting that it allows people to disconnect from their phones and leave feeling good. Her own work includes a sculpture of her brother's tuxedo cat wearing a tuxedo, and she regularly hosts workshops like "paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow." For Masters, the most rewarding aspect of her role is watching students depart fulfilled and enriched by their artistic experience.
